matches.commentary: Ninety-five points in Week 1 — we have seen pub teams manage more — and yet the win goes in the book in permanent ink. Love Thy Naber loved their neighbour right up until kickoff, then learned neighbourliness scores no points. Ugly, necessary, ours.
A Rookie Error by name, a rookie error by nature: chiefly, turning up against a side rounding into ominous form. 133.88 to 126.08. Competitive, respectable, crushed all the same.

We must, regrettably, convene an inquiry. 131.84. 131.86. A margin invisible to the naked eye, felt only in the soul, forever. dpol did not win this so much as the universe quietly mugged us in a car park. We will not be taking questions.

One hundred and forty points, and beaten. Some weeks you do everything right and the man opposite simply rolls a natural twenty. sanfbe rolled a twenty. We tip the cap and grind the teeth — mostly grind the teeth.

After back-to-back gut-punches, the response of champions: no flair, no fireworks, just the quiet ruthless taking-out of the bins. GSac hung around, then was politely shown the door. The ship, gloriously, stops taking on water.
A workmanlike, Tuesday-afternoon-at-the-office victory. No drama, no highlight reel, 115 honest points and a handshake held a fraction too long to be entirely friendly. Benjlev: dispatched.

156.58. Season high. We apologise to absolutely no one. The Brochos arrived with a game plan and left with a learning experience and a 36-point hole where their dignity used to be. This is the tape we show the grandchildren.

The sequel nobody demanded. saulgoat returned for a rematch and received, with interest, the same answer phrased more firmly. Two from two on the season against Naber. Love, it transpires, is not enough.
154.96 — the second 150-burger in three weeks. This team is not in form; it is in a different postcode to form, sending postcards. drjkay never stood a chance and, deep down, knew it.

REVENGE. Capitals entirely deserved. The side that stole 0.02 points and a piece of our soul in Week 3 returned and was beaten by twenty-one. Served cold, served with a small professional smile. We are not over Week 3; we shall simply pretend we are.

Once more unto the breach against sanfbe, and once more a number with no business existing — 160.48. We scored 140 and lost; the second time this nemesis has done it. A rivalry is hereby formally declared. Lawyers have been instructed.

Two hundred and two point three six. Contractually obliged to report it, we refuse to dignify it. Not a fantasy match — a natural disaster with a box score. We put up 133, a winning number on most planets, and were removed from the premises. We never speak of the Week of GSac again.

The wobble. Every champion has one, usually filmed and circulated widely. 95.02, our worst of the year, and Benjlev took the points and the bragging rights. Three losses in four. The obituaries were being typeset — prematurely, as it turned out.

Win and the bye is yours; no pressure beyond the entire complexion of the playoffs. The Brochos, beaten heavily once already, were beaten again — this time with a top-two finish and a week off as the prize. Champions do their best work beside a door marked EXIT.

Rested, ironed, dangerous. The bye did precisely what byes are for. saulgoat, met a third time, made a brief and spirited nuisance of themselves before being escorted firmly into the off-season. Final booked. The throne within touching distance.

And so it ends where it began to ache. dpol — author of the 0.02 — stood between us and the title, scripting so on-the-nose you'd reject it. We led from the first whistle and never let go. The two-hundredths of a point, repaid with twenty-five and change. CHAMPIONS. You may now, finally, speak of Week 3.
